summary: This paper couples instruction-set-level waveform generation to hierarchical equations of motion (HEOM) to study non-perturbative decoherence in superconducting transmons under $1/f$ pure dephasing and compiled control. Y-CPMG exhibits axis-dependent scaling-law breakdown—non-monotonic decoherence and population imbalance ($0.204$ vs $<0.01$)—driven by third-level anharmonicity amplified by bath memory, while X-CPMG maintains power-law scaling with finite-$n$ transient consistent with non-Markovian effects; waveform-level differences remain undetectable across all coupling strengths.
motivation: Superconducting qubit decoherence arises from both multilevel dynamics and structured environmental noise, yet perturbative models cannot capture the resulting signatures when compiled control interacts with non-Markovian baths. Understanding which phenomena emerge from this interplay—and which control details remain invisible to sequence-level observables—requires a framework bridging hardware-faithful waveform generation to beyond-Lindblad open-system dynamics.
method: EmuPlat couples pulse-specification pipelines (four-level intermediate representation from OpenQASM to time-domain waveforms) to rotating-frame HEOM under $1/f$ noise with $\eta \in [7.85 \times 10^{-7}, 5 \times 10^{-6}]$ GHz across three coupling tiers. Two compilation routes (Standard analytical envelopes and VPPU bit-faithful FPGA emulation) feed the same bath model and solver interface, isolating compiled-control–bath-memory interplay while holding device, control architecture, and frame fixed. CPMG scaling is analysed in $\chi$-space ($\chi = -\ln(1-\epsilon)$) to resolve saturation-compressed differences.
result: First-order filter-function theory becomes quantitatively uninformative (>12-order-of-magnitude gap at Ramsey $T_2^*/2$), establishing the non-perturbative baseline. X-CPMG yields $\gamma \approx 1.12$ ($R^2 > 0.99$), marginally exceeding perturbative prediction $\gamma \approx 1$ with finite-$n$ transient absent under matched Lindblad dynamics. Y-CPMG exhibits non-monotonic $\chi(n)$ with peak at $n_\pi = 4$ and partial coherence revival ($R^2 = 0.21$), driven by $\alpha \approx -293$ MHz anharmonicity under finite-duration pulses ($t_\pi \gtrsim 1/|\alpha|$); Standard and VPPU waveforms produce indistinguishable exponents ($|\Delta\gamma| < 10^{-6}$ for X-CPMG, $\chi$-offset $\lesssim 2 \times 10^{-3}$) across all couplings, confirming structural protection by diagonal pure-dephasing operator.
